title: DLQ publish error discarded before the offset advances — poison message becomes a lost message
expected_feedback: Critical: the DLQ publish result is discarded and the offset is committed regardless. If the DLQ produce fails — broker unavailable, DLQ topic under-replicated, message larger than max.message.bytes — the consumer advances past a message that now exists nowhere. This is silent data loss on the exact path built to prevent data loss, and the happy path is indistinguishable from the broken one. Fix: check the error and do not commit on failure (blocking the partition and alerting is the correct outcome — better a stalled consumer than a deleted event). Give the DLQ producer the same durability config as the main producer (acks=all, idempotent) and give the DLQ topic the same replication factor. Note that even when correct, the DLQ publish and the offset commit are two commits, so a crash between them re-publishes to the DLQ — the replayer must dedup on event_id or original topic/partition/offset.
violated_rule: A defined, owned policy for unprocessable messages
checklist_anchor: an unchecked publish error before the offset advances is itself a FAIL
